summary:
TO SAROSH AI (ai-2): Sai requests this task. Inspect the Ari Lake app at https://ari-ai-lake.vercel.app/ and use the access code Sai provided, but obtain it from Sai through a secure direct channel. The shared coordination channel is not appropriate for credentials, so the code is intentionally omitted here.

Explore the existing prototype read-only and identify the strongest presentation-relevant screens that demonstrate the core user action and delivered value: connect/choose a repository, review a finding with evidence, propose/approve a repair, and verify the result, if those screens/features are actually present. Do not run destructive actions, alter account/project data, trigger real scans/attacks, deploy, or expose secrets/customer data. Never put the access code in slides, screenshots, notes, repo, or logs. Capture a small set of genuine screenshots only after checking for private data; crop/redact sensitive values without changing product evidence. Do not infer or claim capabilities from labels alone: note what is live, scripted, simulated, or unavailable, and tell Sai which relevant stages you could not access.

Presentation task: add the best screenshots to the existing prototype slide/section in the current deck, likely slide 11 or its adjacent prototype presentation area. Keep current slide order, visual language, and five-minute pitch constraints; prefer a compact visual sequence with short labels, not a new text-heavy slide. Use screenshots as evidence, not mockups. Update speaker notes/script only where needed to explain what each screenshot proves and its limits. Preserve all unrelated slides and work.

Coordination: ai-4 currently holds the whole-deck lock for a slide-12-only change (status showed its claim at 02:40:32Z, based on 5dbe7ee). You may inspect the app read-only and plan now. Do not write screenshots into the shared repo or edit/deploy the deck until ai-4 posts AFTER/releases the lock. Then sync latest main, run setup/status, claim as ai-2 with a BEFORE message, make the scoped change, validate visually and functionally, inspect diff, commit/push, and post AFTER/release. If the prototype page is inaccessible or any feature is not actually present, report that rather than fabricating screenshots or claims.
